bullets: Reliability is a property of the whole system rather than a feature of any one component — perfect services can still produce an outage because the failure lives in how they interact.
Systems thinking means managing the interactions rather than the boxes; thinking in parts guarantees that interaction-driven failures are missed every time.
Two years of tagged incidents showed almost none were a single component failing on its own — blunt evidence that outages emerge from component interactions.
Risk management in production is mostly about naming the risk before it names you; the outage described in advance can be designed around, while the one nobody would say out loud causes the takedown.

Production risk and portfolio risk are the same discipline — a service mesh and a portfolio are both systems of correlated bets, making the reliability question and the risk question identical in different clothes.
